nonblocking_findings: N1 (docs accuracy, b9362c9d1): the new owner paragraph quotes `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}` as the pattern for the reconcile `--owner` id, but that regex is the accepted-manifest ownerBinding pattern (REVIEWER_ID_PATTERN, v2-manifest-validation.ts:104). The owner value passed with `--owner` lands on staged baseline entries and is validated by OWNER_PATTERN `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$/` (contracts.ts:7, baselineEntrySchema at :81,:313). The adversarial rows prove values the quoted pattern rejects are accepted: `new_debt_accepts_the_owner_value_0wn3r-1d` and `_monorepo_arch` (architecture-v2-route-adversarial.test.ts:798-810). The docs name the wrong contract for the flag they sit next to.

N2 (docs accuracy, same paragraph): 'the preview accepts any `--owner` value' is false when the delta holds new findings. previewArchitectureReconciliation calls createUpdatedArchitectureBaselines (architecture-reconciliation.ts:794-798), and reviewedEntryForFinding parses every new entry through baselineEntrySchema (baseline-update.ts:126-144), refusing a non-conforming owner before any write. The adversarial case title says exactly this ('the owner contract must refuse the value before any write'), and the 1.4d live evidence refused the owner 'Daniel' at the preview (`reconcile_preview_owner_capital=1`). The sentence is true only when no new finding needs the metadata. The underlying behavior is correct and pinned by tests; only the docs sentence overstates.

N3 (evidence wording, minor): the plan line for the renamed-id rows reads 'Both rows failed before the fix (2 failed, 4 skipped)'. The 4 skipped are the gate file's other cases under a name filter, not a state of the code. The green log step 3 describes the same check as a temporary restore of the base production file, so the failing-first property is real; the plan wording alone is ambiguous.

Audit point 1 (gate by path, ae29f456b): stagedManifestFromPreview now matches entry.id === 'reconciliation-manifest' OR entry.repositoryPath === V2_RECONCILIATION_DESTINATION_PATHS[0] (architecture-reconciliation.ts:1186-1190). A preview that renames the id while staging manifest bytes at the manifest path can no longer skip the gate. The first-match edge (a doctored benign entry with the canonical id placed first) cannot reach a write: the acknowledged apply recomputes the canonical preview and requires byte-identity (architecture-reconciliation.ts:1286-1294), so any doctored plan is refused there regardless. The fix is correct defense-in-depth.

Audit point 1 (tests): architecture-review-gate.test.ts gains a manifestId fixture parameter and the case group 'refuses a staged delta under a renamed replacement id' with rows v2-manifest and ownership-map, both asserting the exact gate message. The green log step 3 records the failing-first check (base production restored, the two rows fail). The adversarial file also holds the rows renamed_replacement_id_cannot_complete_a_write with the any-refusal shape; both files pass at HEAD.

Audit point 2 (safe-integer budget, 36925e1f6): after the digit regex, Number(value) must pass Number.isSafeInteger, else the same '--budget-s must be a positive whole number of seconds: <value>' error (architecture-pin-refresh-cli.ts:121-130). The regex accepts a 400-digit string and Number() maps it to Infinity, so the old code set budgetSeconds=Infinity and the budget stop could never fire. The Red case budget_rejects_a_value_that_is_not_a_finite_whole_number (architecture-v2-route-adversarial.test.ts:954-961, committed at the role base 4ec3d5d21) asserts the throw and structurally fails at the base; the green log step 1 records the red run (61 cases, 1 failed). The fix edits no test file.

Verified against the code: the argument parse accepts any --owner value (architecture-reconciliation-cli.ts:146-151 has no pattern check), and enforcement happens in baselineEntrySchema.parse during the preview computation, which both the preview and the acknowledged apply run. Two imprecisions remain; see N1 and N2. Docs only; no behavior change.
